region.text: Holstein under the Danish crown (the Kalmar Union)

ledger.note: 1474: the Duchy of Holstein is held in union with the Danish crown. Christian I of Denmark had been 'proclaimed ... the new Count of Holstein' by the Treaty of Ribe (5 March 1460) and the duchy of 1474 was 'his'; the page speaks of a personal union with Denmark from 1773 to 1864 and of 'the Danish king in his function as duke of Holstein'. The duchy is drawn as a dependency of the Danish crown. [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: the counterpart was kingdom-of-denmark, a dossier of 936-1397/6 that is not alive in 1474; the relation is now chained by the Danish state alive: kalmar-union 1474/2-1523/6, denmark-norway 1523/6-1814/1, kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 1814/1-1864/10. The Danish crown of 1474 is the Kalmar Union of that dossier (Christian I, Oldenburg from 1448).]

6 June 1523: the Kalmar Union ends as the Danish crown's name. The Denmark-Norway page: 'Following Sweden's departure in 1523, the union was effectively dissolved' (infobox 'Gustav Vasa elected King of Sweden: 6 June 1523'), the date the kalmar-union dossier ends on. The page says nothing of Holstein in 1523; that the Danish crown kept Holstein is the Duchy of Holstein page's (king as count and duke from 1460; the Duchy page does not mention 1523 or Frederick I).

region.text: Holstein under the Danish king as duke

ledger.note: 14 January 1814: the Danish kingdom after Kiel holds Holstein as duke. The Duchy of Holstein page: 'After the 1815 Congress of Vienna, the Duchy of Holstein became a member of the German Confederation' and the Danish king ruled 'in his function as duke of Holstein' through stadtholders (a personal union with Denmark to 1864). The date is the Treaty of Kiel's, from the Denmark-Norway page; the relation's end is 30 October 1864.

March 1848: Holstein rises against Denmark. 'In March 1848, the Low German-speaking population of Schleswig, Holstein, and Lauenburg rebelled'; the rebels 'created a provisional government and army' and took the fortress of Rendsburg with the duchies' main armoury (infobox: war begins 24 March 1848). Holstein is the rebels' base on the page; the shape is my reading.

region.text: Holstein, back under the Danish crown

ledger.note: April 1851: Danish rule returns to Holstein. 'On 1 April 1851, the Schleswig-Holstein army was disbanded'; the war ended 'status quo ante bellum', the London Protocol of 8 May 1852 keeping the duchies joined to Denmark by personal union. Cliopatria keeps the rebel shape to 1852.

24 December 1863: the German Confederation executes against the Danish king as duke. 'On 24 December 1863, Saxon and Hanoverian troops marched into Holstein' on the Confederation's behalf (federal execution); Holstein had been a Confederation member since 1815 (Duchy page). Drawn as an occupation by german-confederation. The page does not say when the execution ended.

30 October 1864: the Danish king gives up Holstein. 'Christian IX of Denmark had to renounce both Schleswig and Holstein in the Treaty of Vienna (1864) on October 30.' [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: counterpart changed from kingdom-of-denmark (936-1397/6) to the Danish kingdom alive in 1864, kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940, which records the loss in 1864/10.]

1864: the federal occupation ends (bridging). The Second Schleswig War page does not say when the Saxon and Hanoverian troops left; the end is set to the Treaty of Vienna of 30 October 1864, when kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 records Holstein's cession to german-confederation and austrian-empire.

'Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria' (Treaty of Vienna); the page does not use the word condominium. Drawn as a joint holding (a hatch for each of the two) until the Gastein Convention, as kingdom-of-prussia does (its ledger 1864/10-1865/8, counterpart austrian-empire). region.text: Holstein held jointly by Austria and Prussia

ledger.note: 30 October 1864: the Prussian share of the joint holding (see the Austrian event of the same date). [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: added.]
14 August 1865: the Gastein Convention ends the joint holding; Austria's sole administration follows (next event). 'the Gastein Convention of August 14, 1865'. [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: added.]

14 August 1865: under the Gastein Convention Prussia leaves Holstein to Austria and takes the administration of Schleswig ('Prussia and Austria took over the administration of Schleswig and Holstein respectively'). [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: added.]

14 August 1865: Austria takes over the administration of Holstein. Under 'the Gastein Convention of August 14, 1865' Prussia and Austria took over the administration of Schleswig and Holstein 'respectively': Austria governs Holstein. The land is not annexed.

9 June 1866: Prussia invades Holstein. Prussia declared the Gastein Convention nullified and 'invaded Holstein on 9 June' (Austria had 'decided on 5 June to convene the Diet of Holstein on 11 June'); austrian-empire records the same day as the start of its contest with Prussia. The page does not say when the Austrian administration or troops left, so the Austrian occupation runs on to the Peace of Prague in this ledger and the two hatches overlap June-August. [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: added.]

23 August 1866: the Peace of Prague ends Austria's part in Holstein. The Austro-Prussian War page: the Peace of Prague of 23 August 1866 brought 'the permanent exclusion of Austria from German affairs'; the infobox has Prussia annexing Hanover, Holstein, Schleswig and others. The page does not describe Austria's renunciation of the duchies, nor when Austrian administration ended in practice (probably from the Prussian invasion of 9 June); the date follows austrian-empire's loss of Holstein on 23 August 1866. [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: was year 1866 only, confidence 1, no page.]
24 December 1866: the Prussian occupation becomes annexation: 'annexed both Schleswig and Holstein by decree of December 24, 1866'. [Repair eu-20-l, 2026-11-01: added.]

24 December 1866: Prussia annexes Holstein. The Prussians 'annexed both Schleswig and Holstein by decree of December 24, 1866'; 'The duchy ceased to exist when the Kingdom of Prussia annexed it in 1866 after the Austro-Prussian War.'

notes:
Written for batch eu-20-l (2 pages; budget 1-2). The Cliopatria row 'Duchy of Holstein' has two shapes (1848; 1849-1852), identical (87 cells, 20,119 km2).

WHAT THE CLIOPATRIA SHAPE IS. Not the duchy: it is Holstein plus the south of Schleswig up to 55.3 N, i.e. the territory of the rebel provisional government of 1848-1851 (the First Schleswig War page: the rebels 'drew their base from Holstein ... and the Low German-speaking South of Schleswig'). I therefore corrected both shapes to the Holstein region and wrote the rebel state as a new dossier (provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein, type rebel) which keeps the Cliopatria shape. The duchy-of-schleswig dossier (batch eu-09-x) has no matching loss/gain events for the south of Schleswig in 1848-1851 (its notes say the First Schleswig War is 'not a war entry'); a reviewer should add them with counterpart provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein.

LIFE SPAN. 1474 (14 February, infobox) to 1866 (decree of 24 December 1866); Cliopatria shows only 1848-1852. The new keyframes 1474-1639, 1640-1847, 1853-1866 use the gazetteer's Holstein region; the pages give no outline or area. Not entered: the 1559 conquest of Dithmarschen (recorded by the county-of-holstein dossier, not on the Duchy of Holstein page), the Gottorp share (reunited in 1773 under the Danish king), Altona, Lauenburg (a separate duchy; 'Lauenburg also rebelled' in 1848), the 1806 sovereignty ('gained sovereignty' on the dissolution of the Empire), the 1815 German Confederation (an association), the London Protocol of 1852 (no territorial change). Capital: the infobox gives Glückstadt, which the page says administered the royal shares from 1648; earlier seats are not on the page.

GAZETTEER NAMES WANTED: Pinneberg (9.80E 53.66N) used as a coordinate disc; Dithmarschen; Lauenburg.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIER: county-of-holstein-pinneberg (to 1640, no Cliopatria row). The Danish state is no longer a counterpart without a dossier: see the repair below.

REPAIR eu-20-l, 2026-11-01 (reviewer verdict fail). (a) The notes above were wrong that no Danish rows cover 1474-1864: kalmar-union (1397/6-1523/6), denmark-norway (1526-1814/1) and kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 (1814/1-1940/4) exist, and kingdom-of-denmark (936-1397/6) is not alive in 1474, 1848 or 1864. The vassal relation is chained: kalmar-union 1474/2-1523/6, denmark-norway 1523/6-1814/1, kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 1814/1-1864/10; the two Schleswig wars name kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940. 1523-1526: the relation is drawn as continuous and denmark-norway is named from 6 June 1523 (confidence 1), although that dossier starts in 1526 (its first Cliopatria shape; the page dates the dual monarchy 1536/1537) and kalmar-union ends 6/1523; no page opened shows the Danish crown's hold on Holstein changing. The denmark-norway owner (eu-14-g) should either start in 1523/6 or the renderer should read the chain as unbroken. (b) Thin items taken up: the federal execution of 24 December 1863 (occupation by german-confederation, end 1864/10 at confidence 1: the page is silent); the joint Austro-Prussian holding 30 October 1864-14 August 1865 and Austria's sole administration to 1866 (occupation events for both, pairing the kingdom-of-prussia dossier); the Prussian invasion of 9 June 1866 and the end of the Austrian part on 23 August 1866 (Peace of Prague), the Prussian occupation running to the decree of 24 December 1866. (c) Not entered, with the pages: the 1544 partition of Schleswig and Holstein 'in three parts' and the 1773 reunion of the Gottorp share are shares of one duchy whose outline does not change (the keyframes treat the duchy as one region throughout); the Duchy page does not cover the 1559 conquest of Dithmarschen (the Holstein-Gottorp page was not opened: budget), and the Holstein-Gottorp share has no dossier. ROUTE TO OTHER OWNERS: duchy-of-schleswig (eu-09-x) uses the same dead 'kingdom-of-denmark' counterpart in its 1864 vassal_end; kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 has no vassal relation for Holstein and names duchy-of-holstein for the 1848-1851 loss and gain where the rebel slug is meant; austrian-empire records no occupation of Holstein (only a gain in 1864/10 and a loss in 1866/8); kingdom-of-prussia has the joint holding as occupation of austrian-empire, not of Holstein. Pages opened in the repair beyond the original budget of 1-2: 3 new and 1 reopened.

Fix fx-45 (2 Nov 2026), Denmark-Norway. The vassal_start of 6 June 1523 with counterpart denmark-norway and its vassal_end of 14 January 1814 were removed. Denmark-Norway is not alive until 1526, so the compile read the start with Holstein as the suzerain and drew the whole Denmark-Norway realm (2,934 cells) as Holstein's vassal; window p1500-p1599 closed it in 1526 by a patch event, and the dossier no longer depends on that patch. The Duchy of Holstein page gives no overlordship of Denmark over Holstein or the reverse for these years: infobox 'State of the Holy Roman Empire (1474-1806)' and 'Personal union with the Kingdom of Denmark (1474-1544; 1773-1864)'; 'Members of the Danish House of Oldenburg ruled Holstein - jointly with the Duchy of Schleswig - for its entire existence'; the royal part after the 1544 partition was 'held by Christian III and his successors (identical with the Kings of Denmark)'. The page says nothing dated 1526 or 1814 for Holstein. Holstein's land from 1526 to 1814 is drawn by denmark-norway's shape as in Cliopatria; the relation before 1523 (kalmar-union) and after 1814 (kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940) is unchanged, and hierarchy.csv keeps the Holy Roman Empire membership.
